en.name: Instant dashi
en.summary: Instant dashi comes as granules in a jar, tea-bag style sachets of ground kombu and bonito, or a concentrated liquid in a bottle. Dry forms keep about 12 months in a cool dry cupboard. Once you make it up into stock it is stock: 3–4 days in the fridge.
en.pantry: Dry granules and sealed sachets keep about 12 months from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard — a figure taken from the dry soup-mix and bouillon line, not one published for dashi. Airtight is the whole game: the granules are hygroscopic and cake into a solid lump the moment they meet humidity, which is how most jars of instant dashi actually end in a humid kitchen. Keep them away from the kettle, the rice cooker and the hob, and never shake damp granules back into the jar.
en.fridge: The dry product does not belong in the fridge; moving it in and out drives condensation into the powder. Once made up into liquid stock, though, it is stock: covered, at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, 3–4 days. Concentrated liquid dashi in a bottle should be refrigerated after opening and used to the maker's instruction — the printed best-before date stops applying once a prepacked product is opened.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for the dry product and freezing a hygroscopic powder is a bad idea: every trip out of the freezer invites condensation. Made-up dashi is a different matter and freezes like any stock — ice-cube trays at −18 °C (0 °F) are the practical form. But if you have instant dashi in the cupboard, there is rarely any reason to freeze stock at all; you can make what you need in a minute.
en.thawing: Thaw frozen made-up dashi in the fridge or drop the cubes straight into a hot pan. Do not thaw it on the counter.
spoilage: Granules caked into a hard lump that will not break up
A stale or fishy-rancid smell rather than a clean smoky-marine one
Made-up stock that smells sour or has a film on the surface
tips: Use a dry spoon and close the jar immediately; humidity is the enemy.
Keep granules away from steam sources — kettle, rice cooker, hob.
Refrigerate opened liquid concentrate and follow the bottle.
Buy small jars if you cook Japanese food only occasionally.

faq.q: How long does instant dashi last?
faq.a: About 12 months from purchase for dry granules and sealed sachets, kept airtight in a cool dry cupboard.

faq.q: How long does made-up dashi keep?
faq.a: 3–4 days covered in the fridge at 4 °C or below, the same as any prepared stock.

faq.q: Does liquid dashi concentrate need refrigerating?
faq.a: Yes, after opening, and follow the maker's instruction. The printed date stops applying once the bottle is opened.

faq.q: Why did my dashi granules turn into a solid lump?
faq.a: They absorbed moisture from the air. Store them airtight away from steam and use a dry spoon each time.

zh.name: 日式高湯粉／高湯包
zh.summary: 即溶日式高湯有罐裝顆粒、像茶包一樣的高湯包，以及瓶裝濃縮液三種形式。乾燥形式放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃大約 12 個月。一旦沖泡成高湯，它就是高湯：冷藏 3～4 天。
zh.pantry: 乾燥顆粒和未拆封的高湯包放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算大約 12 個月——這個數字取自「乾燥湯粉與高湯塊」的資料，不是專為日式高湯發表的。關鍵全在密封：顆粒吸濕性強，碰到濕氣就會結成一整塊，而這正是台灣這種潮濕廚房裡一罐柴魚粉真正的結局。請遠離熱水壺、電鍋和爐火，也不要把受潮的顆粒抖回罐子裡。
zh.fridge: 乾燥品不該放冰箱；反覆進出會把冷凝水帶進粉裡。但沖泡成液體高湯之後，它就是高湯：加蓋、放 4 °C 以下，3～4 天。瓶裝的濃縮高湯露開封後要冷藏，並依廠商指示使用——預先包裝的產品一旦開封，標示的有效日期就不再適用。
zh.freezer: 乾燥品沒有冷凍期限，而且冷凍吸濕性粉末並不明智：每次拿進拿出都在招來冷凝水。沖泡好的高湯則不同，冷凍方式和一般高湯一樣——用製冰盒在 −18 °C 凍成小塊最實用。不過既然櫥櫃裡就有高湯粉，其實很少有理由去冷凍高湯，要用時一分鐘就能泡好。
zh.thawing: 冷凍的高湯塊請放冷藏解凍，或直接丟進熱鍋。不要放室溫解凍。
spoilage: 顆粒結成敲不散的硬塊
聞起來有陳味或魚油走味的味道，而不是乾淨的燻香海味
高湯包受潮、變色或結塊
沖好的高湯發酸，或表面結了一層膜
tips: 用乾燥的湯匙，取完立刻蓋緊；濕氣是頭號敵人。
遠離蒸氣來源——熱水壺、電鍋、爐台。
開封的濃縮高湯露要冷藏，並照瓶身指示使用。
偶爾才做日式料理的話，請買小罐。

faq.q: 日式高湯粉可以放多久？
faq.a: 乾燥顆粒和未拆的高湯包密封放陰涼乾燥處，從購買日起算大約 12 個月。

faq.q: 泡好的日式高湯可以放多久？
faq.a: 加蓋冷藏在 4 °C 以下 3～4 天，和其他現成高湯一樣。
開封後要，並依廠商指示使用。瓶身標示的日期在開封後就不再適用。

faq.q: 柴魚粉為什麼結成一塊？
faq.a: 它從空氣中吸了水。請密封、遠離蒸氣，每次都用乾燥的湯匙。
